unit_label: CB Appendices 1 to 5: committees set up by RBI, international financial institutions, crypto currencies and CBDC, sustainable finance and glossary

facts.statement: Committees table (courseware Appendix 1, important committees; subject): A.K. Bhuchar - coordination between commercial banks and term lending institutions; Bimal Jalan panel - scrutinising applications for new bank licences; Deepak Mohanty Committee - management of data and information in the RBI; Abid Hussain Committee - smaller industries; Aditya Puri Committee - dissemination of information related to credit; James Raj Committee - functioning of public sector banks; Bhandari Committee - reconstruction of the RRBs; Bhide Committee - coordination between SFCs and commercial banks; C. Rangarajan Committee - eliminating the poverty scale of the country; Cook Committee - capital adequacy of banks; Damodaran Committee - improving customer services in banks; S.N. Verma Committee (1999) - restructuring of commercial banks; Deepak Parekh Committee - financing the infrastructure sector; Dinesh Sharma Committee - proposing new regulation related to virtual or digital currencies; Suma Verma Committee - revising and updating the Banking Ombudsman Scheme, 2006; Tandon Committee - processing for credit and working capital assessment; Narasimham Committee - reforms related to the banking sector; Parthasarathi Shome Committee - implementation of the General Anti Avoidance Rule (GAAR); R. Jilani Committee - the banking inspection system; R.H. Khan Committee - harmonising the role of financial institutions; R.S. Gujral Committee - measures to boost MSME exports; S.P. Talwar Committee - restructuring the weak public sector banks; A.C. Shah Committee - NBFC reforms; A. Ghosh Committee - malpractices and frauds in India; A.K. Khandelwal Committee - HR related issues of public sector banks; K.M. Chandrasekhar Committee - rationalising the foreign investment norms; Vaghul Committee - India money market; R.V. Gupta Committee - small savings; K.V. Kamath panel - Expert Committee on resolution framework for Covid-19 related issues.
facts.locator: S05 courseware Appendix 1, printed pp. 459-460 (PDF pp. 476-477), table of important committees

facts.statement: International financial institutions (courseware Appendix 2): the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is headquartered in Washington, D.C.; it was formed in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference primarily by the ideas of Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes and came into formal existence in 1945 with 29 member countries; its goals include fostering global monetary cooperation, securing financial stability, facilitating international trade, promoting high employment and sustainable economic growth, and reducing poverty; countries contribute funds to a pool from which countries experiencing balance of payments difficulties can borrow; the major functional roles of the IMF are surveillance, financial assistance to facilitate adjustment and technical assistance; the programmes include the stand-by arrangements (SBA) for short-term stabilisation and the structural adjustment programme for medium-term adjustment; the facilities include the Extended Fund Facility (EFF), Supplementary Financing Facility (SFF), Poverty Reduction and Growth Facility (PRGF), Stand-by Arrangement, Compensatory Financing Facility (CFF), Emergency Assistance and the Exogenous Shock Facility; the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) offers loans to middle income developing countries, is the first of five member institutions that compose the World Bank Group, is headquartered in Washington, D.C., was established in 1944 with the mission of financing the reconstruction of European nations devastated by World War II, and its concessional lending arm is the International Development Association; the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is an international financial institution owned by central banks, serves as a bank for central banks, was established on 17 May 1930 by an intergovernmental agreement between Germany, Belgium, France, the United Kingdom, Italy, Japan, the United States and Switzerland, and opened in Basel, Switzerland; it was originally intended to facilitate reparations imposed on Germany by the Treaty of Versailles (the Young Loan); the G10 Governors created the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision after the collapse of Bankhaus Herstatt (1974).
facts.locator: S05 courseware Appendix 2, printed pp. 461-462 (PDF pp. 478-479), sections 1 to 3

facts.statement: IFSC operations of Indian banks (courseware Appendix 2 section 4): the Reserve Bank issued instructions on 01.12.2022 (RBI/2022-23/145, dated December 1, 2022) to Indian banks and All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs) on dealing in financial products by their branches and subsidiaries operating outside India, and on the applicability of these instructions to International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs) in India including Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City); foreign branches or subsidiaries of Indian banks and AIFIs can deal in financial products, including structured financial products, which are not available or not permitted by the Reserve Bank in the domestic market without prior approval of the Reserve Bank, subject to compliance with conditions and those prescribed by the host regulator; the branches and subsidiaries of Indian banks and AIFIs operating in IFSCs may also deal in such products subject to conditions; the financial products dealt with shall attract prudential norms such as capital adequacy, exposure norms (including the Large Exposure Framework), periodical valuation and other applicable norms; the parent bank shall adhere to the more stringent of the host and home regulations in respect of prudential norms; if the current norms of the Reserve Bank do not specify prudential treatment of any financial product, the parent bank or AIFI shall seek specific guidance from the Reserve Bank.
facts.locator: S05 courseware Appendix 2 section 4, printed p. 463 (PDF p. 480)

facts.statement: Crypto currencies, central bank view (courseware Appendix 3): the preamble of the RBI Act states the purpose of regulating the issue of bank notes and keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability; the major functional roles of the Reserve Bank are monopoly of note issue, banker to banks, banker to Government and regulation and supervision of the financial system; crypto currencies are internet-based transactions using distributed ledger technology (DLT) and the blockchain process; the first crypto currency, bitcoin, was created by using the blockchain process in 2008 and its genesis is attributed to Satoshi Nakamoto; on a blockchain each new block is validated and added to the previous chain of blocks, and double spending is difficult because it would involve changing every subsequent block; the Ministry of Finance of the Government of India undertook the imposition of 30 per cent tax on all crypto transactions; the Inter-Ministerial Committee has recommended banning cryptocurrencies; the courseware argues that cryptocurrencies are not akin to financial instruments because a currency has an issuer, usually a trusted entity such as the sovereign; crypto currencies do not satisfy any of the attributes of money (medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value and standard of deferred payments); stablecoins pegged to official currencies are a concern; crypto currencies bypass KYC, AML and CFT arrangements which makes them attractive for illegal transactions; the courseware concludes that banning cryptocurrency is perhaps the most advisable choice and that the Government should continue to contain the spread through taxation.
facts.locator: S05 courseware Appendix 3, printed pp. 464-472 (PDF pp. 481-489), sections 1 to 10

facts.statement: Central bank digital currency (courseware Appendix 3 section 11): central banks are trying to reap the benefits of blockchain and DLT by the introduction of CBDC; a CBDC is pegged to the value of the country fiat currency, is the digital form of a country fiat currency, is issued and regulated by a nation monetary authority or central bank, promotes financial inclusion and simplifies the implementation of monetary and fiscal policy; as a centralised form of currency CBDCs may not anonymise transactions as some cryptocurrencies do; the Annual Economic Review of the BIS makes the case for CBDC designs that preserve the central bank role in the payment system; CBDCs should be best designed as part of a two-tier scheme, with the central bank operating the core of the system and private sector firms delegated consumer-facing activities; an account based or token based design is considered; the budget for 2022 announced that the Reserve Bank of India would introduce the Central Bank Digital Currency; the RBI launched the wholesale version of CBDC on 1 November 2022 and the retail version on 1 December 2022 on pilot basis; so-called multi-CBDC (mCBDC) arrangements across borders could improve cross-border payments.
facts.locator: S05 courseware Appendix 3 section 11 and the sum up, printed pp. 472-475 (PDF pp. 489-492)

facts.statement: Sustainable finance (courseware Appendix 4): the Sustainable Finance Group (SFG) in the Department of Regulation of the Reserve Bank carried out a survey in January 2022 on the status of climate risk and sustainable finance in leading scheduled commercial banks; key observations: board-level engagement was inadequate (in about a third of banks responsibility for overseeing climate risk initiatives was yet to be assigned and only a few banks have included climate or ESG KPIs in the performance evaluation of top management); a majority of banks did not have a separate business unit for sustainability; only a few banks had a strategy for embedding ESG principles; physical and transition risks were seen as the main sources of climate-related risks; most banks decided to gradually reduce exposure to high-carbon emitting businesses; a majority of banks have not aligned their climate-related financial disclosures with any internationally accepted framework; most banks felt the available data was insufficient; suggestions to banks include board or top management oversight and ESG KPIs in performance evaluation, full grasp of physical, transition and liability risks, aligning disclosures with an internationally accepted framework, mobilising new capital for green lending, investing in capacity building and moving to a low-carbon operating strategy in line with India commitment at the COP26 summit with a timeline for net-zero emissions; the reference is the Survey on Climate Risk and Sustainable Finance, July 2022, by the Sustainable Finance Group, Department of Regulation, RBI.
facts.locator: S05 courseware Appendix 4, printed pp. 476-478 (PDF pp. 493-495)

facts.statement: Glossary extracts (courseware Appendix 5): Automated Clearing House (ACH) is a computerised facility used by member depository institutions to electronically combine, sort and distribute inter-bank credits and debits; Bank Identifier Code (BIC) is an ISO technical code that uniquely identifies a financial institution, with SWIFT as the registration authority, and consists of eight or eleven characters made up of a bank code (four characters), a country code (two characters), a location code (two characters) and, optionally, a branch code (three characters); Bank Rate is defined under Section 49 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 as the standard rate at which the Bank is prepared to buy or rediscount bills of exchange or other commercial paper eligible for purchase under the Act; a bank run is a series of unexpected cash withdrawals caused by a sudden decline in depositor confidence; the call money rate is the rate at which short term funds are borrowed and lent in the inter-bank call money market, where the duration of the call money loan is 1 day (overnight); a haircut is a risk control measure applied to underlying assets whereby the value of those assets is calculated as the market value reduced by a certain percentage; Infinet (Indian Financial Network) is a satellite based wide area network using VSAT technology set up by the RBI in June 1999, with the hub and the Network Management System located in the Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology (IDRBT) Hyderabad; inflation targeting is a monetary policy that focuses on assigning a single objective of keeping inflation at a targeted level or within a band, adopted by central banks of countries like Australia, New Zealand and Canada; the key rate is the interest rate that controls, directly or indirectly, bank lending rates and the cost of credit paid by borrowers; the Humphrey-Hawkins Act is the informal name for the Full Employment and Balanced Growth Act of 1978; the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision is an international committee of bank supervisors associated with the Bank for International Settlements headquartered in Basel.
facts.locator: S05 courseware Appendix 5 glossary, printed pp. 479-488 (PDF pp. 496-505) selected entries

payload.expanded_explanation_md: The list is a courseware table; the unit does not say who appointed each body.

self_check.prompt_text: Which committee looked at the banking inspection system?

payload.title: IMF, IBRD and BIS
payload.core_explanation_md:
**IMF:** Washington, D.C.; **Bretton Woods 1944**, formal in **1945**; roles: **surveillance, financial assistance, technical assistance**; facilities include **EFF, SFF, PRGF, Stand-by, CFF, Emergency Assistance, Exogenous Shock Facility**.

**IBRD:** loans to **middle income developing countries**; first of **five** World Bank Group institutions; concessional arm is the **IDA**.

**BIS:** **17 May 1930**, **Basel**; a **bank for central banks**; created the **BCBS** after **Herstatt (1974)**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Each institution has a different client: IMF serves balance of payments needs, IBRD funds development projects, and BIS serves central banks.

payload.title: Overseas and IFSC operations of banks
payload.core_explanation_md: The RBI instruction of **1 December 2022** lets foreign branches and subsidiaries of Indian banks and **AIFIs** (including those in **IFSCs such as GIFT City**) deal in products **not permitted domestically**, subject to **RBI conditions** and the **host regulator**. **Capital adequacy, exposure norms (including the Large Exposure Framework) and valuation** apply, and the parent follows the **more stringent** of home and host rules.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: If RBI norms do not give the prudential treatment of a product, the parent seeks specific RBI guidance.

self_check.prompt_text: Whose prudential rule applies to an overseas product: home or host?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The more stringent of the two.

payload.title: The central bank view of crypto currencies
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Genesis:** **bitcoin** from **2008**, attributed to **Satoshi Nakamoto**, using **blockchain/DLT**.

**Courseware arguments:** a currency needs an **issuer** and the attributes of money; crypto is neither currency, asset nor instrument; it **bypasses KYC/AML/CFT**; stablecoins raise concern.

**Policy view:** the note concludes that a **ban** is perhaps the most advisable, with **taxation** (30 per cent on transfers) used to contain spread.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: These are the courseware arguments and the policy position as stated by the note.

self_check.prompt_text: What are the four functions of money the note tests crypto against?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A medium of exchange, a measure of value, a store of value and a standard for deferred payments.

payload.title: Central bank digital currency
payload.core_explanation_md:
**CBDC:** **digital form of fiat currency**, **issued by the central bank**, **promotes financial inclusion**; a **centralised** form that may not give **anonymity**.

**Design:** a **two-tier** scheme with the central bank at the core and private firms at the customer interface.

**India:** announced in the **budget for 2022**; **wholesale pilot 1 November 2022**; **retail pilot 1 December 2022**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: mCBDC arrangements could make cross-border payments better but raise currency substitution concerns.

self_check.prompt_text: When was the retail CBDC pilot launched?

payload.title: Sustainable finance survey
payload.core_explanation_md:
The **SFG** survey (**January 2022**) found **inadequate board-level engagement**, no separate sustainability unit in most banks, **physical and transition risks** as main sources of climate risk, and **disclosures not aligned** with an international framework.

**Suggestions:** board oversight and ESG KPIs, integrate climate risk into risk management, align disclosures, mobilise green capital, build capacity, plan **net-zero** operations (COP26).
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The survey informs how the RBI shapes its supervisory approach to climate risk.

self_check.prompt_text: Which two kinds of risk did banks see as the main climate-related sources?

payload.title: Glossary extracts
payload.core_explanation_md: **BIC:** **8 or 11 characters** (bank 4, country 2, location 2, branch 3 optional), **SWIFT** is the registration authority. **Bank Rate:** **Section 49** of the RBI Act, standard rate to **rediscount** eligible bills. **Call money:** **overnight** inter-bank lending. **Haircut:** market value **reduced by a percentage**. **Infinet:** **June 1999**, **VSAT**, hub at **IDRBT Hyderabad**. **Inflation targeting:** one **objective** of keeping inflation at a target or band.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The glossary covers many more terms; this batch itemises only these.

self_check.prompt_text: How many characters can a BIC have?
